findings.title: "Silence notifications" does nothing in the new list view
findings.body: In the list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` now passes only `promRule` (GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47), so `rule` is undefined here. `AlertRuleMenu` still shows the Silence item, because `canSilence` is true through `grafanaSilenceAbility` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:96, 126-132). Clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`, but the drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and with `rule` undefined it never is. The user clicks a visible menu item and nothing happens: no drawer, no error. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test only checks that the item exists (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:194) and never clicks it. Fix: open the drawer from the prom rule when the ruler rule is missing (or pass the rule UID to the drawer), or hide the item until the drawer can open.

findings.title: Pause and Delete are gone from the Grafana rule list menu even when the user has permission
findings.body: This PR computes `canPause` and `canDelete` from the prom-rule abilities (lines 83, 87). The menu items, though, still need a ruler rule: Pause needs `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and Delete needs `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). The list view no longer has a ruler rule (GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47 passes only `promRule`), so both items disappear for every Grafana rule in GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView. Before this PR, GrafanaRuleLoader passed `rule={rulerRule}` and both actions were available. The new test locks this in by expecting exactly 4 items (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:205-207) while it grants AlertingRuleUpdate and AlertingRuleDelete. If dropping these actions is intended, the PR description should say so. If not, Delete can be driven by the GrafanaRuleIdentifier built in `getEditableIdentifier`, and Pause needs a prom-rule-based path.

findings.title: Rule view link lost its `returnTo` parameter
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()` (old GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx). The new component drops it. Users who open a rule from a filtered or searched list no longer return to that list state from the rule view; they land on the default list. Restore `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and pass `{ returnTo }` again.

findings.title: Comment's reason for the More button doesn't match the menu
findings.body: The test says the More button stays "for other actions like viewing", but the menu has no View item. It stays because Copy link is always shown. The test also never checks that Delete/Pause are hidden or that Silence opens a drawer, so it would not catch either regression above.

contracts.action: Click "Silence notifications" in the list-view More menu for a Grafana rule
contracts.equivalent_path: Old GrafanaRuleLoader passed rule={rulerRule}, so the drawer rendered with that ruler rule
contracts.before_after: Before: the drawer opened. After: the state flag is set but the drawer's render condition needs a ruler rule, which the list view no longer has

contracts.action: Open the More menu in the list view (Pause/Delete visibility)
contracts.equivalent_path: The same menu in the rule viewer, which has a rulerRule
contracts.before_after: canPause/canDelete come from prom abilities, but the items still need rulerRule
contracts.visible_effect: Pause and Delete are hidden for all Grafana rules in the list

contracts.action: Edit button permission from the prom rule's folder (useFolder)
contracts.before_after: While the folder loads, MaybeSupported is NotSupported, so the button stays hidden until the folder arrives
contracts.visible_effect: The Edit button appears after the folder metadata loads
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder fetch fails, `folder` stays undefined, so isEditable is false and the Edit button stays hidden without an error
contracts.open_question: Does useFolder surface fetch errors anywhere the user can see?

summary: The list view no longer calls the ruler API, but the action components still need a ruler rule in some places. As a result, three things regress in the Grafana rule list: the Silence item does nothing when clicked, Pause and Delete no longer appear even when the user has permission, and the rule view link loses its `returnTo` parameter. The new tests check that the More menu has exactly 4 items, which makes the missing Pause and Delete look intended. Not reviewed: whether `useFolder` shows fetch errors to the user (left open).
